items.headline: WP MP Jamus Lim hospitalised with pneumonia after a bout of influenza
items.summary: Workers' Party Sengkang GRC MP Jamus Lim was hospitalised over the weekend with pneumonia after what began as Influenza A, with his blood-oxygen level dipping into the low 90s. He said he would miss his regular duties, including a Meet-the-People Session, while he recovers.

items.headline: Singapore may shut schools if next-day PSI is forecast to top 300 as haze bites
items.summary: Education Minister Desmond Lee said MOE would consider closing schools and postponing exams if the next day's 24-hour PSI is forecast to enter the hazardous range above 300. The central-area reading hit 168 on 10 October and NEA warned the PSI could pass 200; student-care and kindergarten-care centres will stay open even if schools close.

items.headline: Singapore's 2026 Grand Prix drew 301,294 fans, the second-highest crowd on record
items.summary: Organisers said the 2026 Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix drew 301,294 spectators across the race weekend, the second-highest attendance since the night race began in 2008 and just shy of the 2022 record of about 302,000, achieved despite the haze.

items.headline: Chinese tourist's Louis Vuitton bag stolen at Gardens by the Bay by a fake helper
items.summary: A Chinese tourist had her Louis Vuitton bag stolen at Gardens by the Bay after asking a passer-by for directions, only for that person to turn out to be the thief, Mothership reported.

items.headline: India's retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September, above forecasts
items.summary: India's consumer-price inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September, above analysts' estimates and well above the Reserve Bank's 4% target midpoint, as the oil spike from the Middle East war and a weak monsoon pushed up energy and food costs. The reading reinforces the RBI's recent rate hike.

items.headline: Reliance's Jio sets IPO price band for what will be India's largest-ever listing
items.summary: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms set its IPO price band at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share, valuing the telecom operator at as much as 10.3 trillion rupees (about $107 billion) and raising roughly 302 billion rupees. The offering is on track to become India's largest-ever IPO, eclipsing Hyundai Motor India's $3.3 billion.

items.headline: Update: Rupee rebounds as the RBI draws a line in the sand at 97 per dollar
items.summary: The rupee rose more than 1% on Monday, pulling away from the 97-per-dollar level after the Reserve Bank's special oil-dollar window and tighter hedging rules, among its strongest interventions since the 2013 taper tantrum. The currency had neared May's record low of 96.9650.

items.headline: Update: India's opposition marches to the Supreme Court to demand the election chief's removal
items.summary: Opposition parties led by the Congress marched to the Supreme Court demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a disputed voter-roll revision they call vote theft, days after the court ruled the earlier detention of protesters illegal.

items.headline: Burnham blames Iran for an RAF Fairford plot and sanctions two Iranians
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told Parliament that a suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford was almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and he announced sanctions on two Iranian nationals.

items.headline: Burnham tells MPs Britain will renegotiate parts of its post-Brexit deal with the EU
items.summary: Burnham told the Commons that the UK would renegotiate elements of its post-Brexit trade arrangement with the European Union, with a bilateral summit in Brussels set for November covering immigration cooperation, a youth-mobility scheme and emissions trading.

items.headline: Burnham and Healey meet business leaders ahead of a tough October budget
items.summary: Burnham and Chancellor John Healey met business leaders to ease concern over possible tax rises before the 28 October budget, which Burnham has called challenging as Middle East energy prices stoke inflation.

items.headline: Burnham races to plug a multi-billion-pound hole in his flagship care plan
items.summary: Burnham has tasked senior officials with finding ways to fill a multi-billion-pound funding gap in his flagship plan for a new national care service, a shortfall that risks delaying the policy.

items.headline: Houthis strike Riyadh's main airport again as Trump weighs joining the fight
items.summary: A second strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed one person and injured 11 on Sunday, after Saturday's deadlier attack left 12 dead and more than 300 wounded. The airport has been shut since Saturday, and President Trump said he is weighing whether to join the fight against the Houthis.

items.headline: Nobel economics prize goes to Robert Hall and Michael Woodford
items.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Stanford's Robert E. Hall and Columbia's Michael Woodford for work on the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization, models now used by central banks worldwide. They share the 12-million-krona (about $1.2 million) award.

items.headline: Update: Zelensky says Russia already broke Trump's surprise energy ceasefire
items.summary: Zelensky said Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant hours after Trump announced an energy truce, telling the Warsaw Security Forum that Putin does not read Truth Social. Trump separately said it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, which Zelensky rejected while the war continues.

items.headline: Pope Leo XIV to have surgery to remove an early-stage lung nodule
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV, 71, said he would undergo surgery at Rome's Gemelli hospital to remove an early-stage nodule found on his left lung during a routine checkup. Papal audiences are cancelled through 20 October, and he still hopes to make a November trip to Latin America.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI model
items.summary: Meta's Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder, which it describes as its first frontier model, larger and more capable than the earlier lightweight Muse Spark. It is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens through the Meta Model API.

items.headline: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with business customers
items.summary: At a Google Cloud event, Google launched a unified Gemini agent for businesses that can take multi-step actions and optionally run on Anthropic's Claude models, with a consumer rollout to follow. Sundar Pichai said Gemini has more than 1 billion monthly active users.

items.headline: Google opens a public SynthID site to flag AI-generated media
items.summary: Google launched a public SynthID verification site that lets anyone check whether an image, video or audio clip was made with AI. OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao also support the watermarking standard.

items.headline: Asos confirms a customer-data breach after hackers hijack its app alerts
items.summary: UK retailer Asos confirmed in a London Stock Exchange filing that hackers accessed a third-party platform holding customer data and pushed a rogue app notification demanding engagement or a leak. Names and contact details were taken, and Asos shares fell more than 10%.

items.headline: US stocks waver before bank earnings as a chip selloff drags the Nasdaq
items.summary: US stocks hovered near records on Monday as a 2.7% slide in a gauge of chipmakers offset optimism before third-quarter bank earnings, with trading volume the lowest of 2026. Analysts expect S&P 500 profits to have grown by roughly 25% to 30% from a year earlier.

items.headline: Update: Oil holds near $107 Brent as an expanding Middle East war threatens supply
items.summary: Oil extended its advance, with Brent near $107 a barrel and WTI around $93 after a 2.1% jump, as Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and doubts over Trump's Russia-Ukraine energy truce stoked fears over supply.

items.headline: US mortgage-bond funds suffer one of their worst outflows since 2021
items.summary: Investors pulled money from US mortgage-bond funds at one of the fastest paces since 2021 over the past three weeks, Bloomberg reported, as a spike in Treasury yields to multi-decade highs, driven by surging oil prices and inflation worries, hammered the securities.

items.headline: Paramount Skydance completes its roughly $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery takeover
items.summary: Paramount Skydance completed its roughly $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating a new Hollywood giant that must manage about $80 billion in debt and is targeting $6 billion in cost savings over three years.

items.headline: Antonelli closes on the F1 title and can clinch it at the US Grand Prix in Austin
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 drivers' standings by 102 points over Mercedes teammate George Russell with six rounds to go, after finishing third at the Singapore Grand Prix. By the series' points maths he could seal his first world title at the US Grand Prix in Austin on 23-25 October if he outscores Russell by 23 points and Lewis Hamilton by 14.

items.headline: Bergs stuns Alcaraz in Shanghai, securing year-end No. 1 for Zverev
items.summary: Belgium's Zizou Bergs beat world No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6(4) at the Shanghai Masters for the biggest win of his career. Alcaraz's exit confirmed that Alexander Zverev will finish 2026 as the ATP year-end World No. 1.

items.headline: Tsitsipas beats Fritz to set up a Shanghai fourth-round clash with Medvedev
items.summary: Stefanos Tsitsipas beat Taylor Fritz to reach the Shanghai Masters fourth round, where he will face fifth seed and 2019 champion Daniil Medvedev.

items.headline: Arthur Gea upsets Ben Shelton to reach the Shanghai fourth round
items.summary: France's Arthur Gea upset Ben Shelton to reach the fourth round of the Shanghai Masters, one of several seeds to fall early at the tournament.

items.headline: Physicists build the first working thorium-229 nuclear clock
items.summary: A team at TU Wien reported the first working thorium-229 optical nuclear clock, stabilising a laser to the nucleus's 148-nanometre transition and running it unattended for a day; a China-led group published a parallel result in Nature. Nuclear clocks could eventually outperform today's atomic standards and sharpen tests of fundamental physics.

items.headline: Mathematicians unveil a 3D 'einstein' tile that fills space without repeating
items.summary: Researchers announced a three-dimensional aperiodic monotile, dubbed Chair44, that can fill space with a pattern that never repeats, the 3D successor to the 2023 two-dimensional hat tile. The AI-assisted result, from Automorph's Ioannis Tsiokos, has not yet been peer-reviewed.

items.headline: A new brain study probes why cannabis can trigger paranoia
items.summary: A new brain-imaging study investigated why cannabis provokes anxiety and paranoia in some people, pointing to how THC alters activity in the regions that govern threat perception.

items.headline: Woody 'blankets' are laid on Arctic permafrost to keep its carbon locked away
items.summary: A Canadian start-up, PermaC, completed the first field test of insulating blankets of woody material over a rapidly eroding permafrost site in the Northwest Territories, aiming to stop the carbon dioxide and methane released when thaw slumps expose ancient soil. Researchers say it is the first approach aimed at preventing permafrost thaw itself.

fun_fact.headline: Bluetooth is named after a 10th-century Viking king
fun_fact.body: Bluetooth wireless technology is named after Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson, the 10th-century Danish king who unified Denmark - a nod to uniting devices and protocols. Its logo is a bind rune that merges the king's initials, Hagall and Bjarkan, from the runic alphabet. The name started life as a 1996 codename proposed by an Intel engineer and simply stuck.

puzzle.title: Gear Train
puzzle.body: Five gears are meshed tooth-to-tooth in a straight row: A-B-C-D-E. You turn gear A clockwise. (1) Which way does gear E turn? (2) Now the same five gears are arranged in a closed ring, each meshed with its two neighbours (A-B-C-D-E and back to A). You try to turn gear A clockwise. What happens?
puzzle.approach: Meshed gears always turn in opposite directions; trace the alternation along the row, then ask whether a closed loop has an odd or even number of gears.
puzzle.answer: (1) Gear E turns clockwise - meshed gears alternate direction, so A clockwise makes B counter-clockwise, C clockwise, D counter-clockwise and E clockwise. (2) Nothing turns; the ring jams. In a closed loop each gear must spin opposite to both neighbours, which is only possible with an even number of gears. With five (odd) the alternation contradicts itself, so the gears lock.

word_puzzle.title: The Full Dozen
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed square - TOP: I O L; RIGHT: A T E; BOTTOM: D G R; LEFT: C N S. Chain words so each new word begins with the previous word's last letter; consecutive letters must come from different sides; use all 12 letters. Solve in two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain words corner to corner and cover all 12 letters; never use two letters from the same side in a row.
word_puzzle.answer: DIAGNOSTIC then CRADLE. DIAGNOSTIC runs D-I-A-G-N-O-S-T-I-C with no two consecutive letters sharing a side, ending in C; CRADLE begins with C and runs C-R-A-D-L-E. Together they use all twelve letters A, C, D, E, G, I, L, N, O, R, S, T.
